title: No Differences Between 12 Weeks of Block- vs. Traditional-Periodized Training in Performance Adaptations in Trained Cyclists
claims: The study compared 12 weeks of load-matched block periodization (n = 14) with traditional periodization (n = 16) in trained cyclists with peak oxygen uptake of 58 ± 8 ml·kg−1·min−1.
No group differences were found in time-trial performances or in most muscular and hematological adaptations.
Red blood cell volume increased 10 ± 16% more in the block group, while capillaries around type I fibers increased 20 ± 12% more in the traditional group.
Both groups improved 5-minute and 40-minute time-trial power by 9 ± 9% and 8 ± 9%, respectively.
The authors concluded that there was no difference in performance between block periodization and a best-practice traditional periodization using a cyclic, progressively increasing training load.
